messages:
liam: FYI cluster autoscaler reports attach waits in ap-southeast1 while a deep-scrub job hit hot NVMes. GPU pods queued for ~5m.

sophie: ouch. which janitor/scrub ran? we scheduled deep-scrub for 03:00 but autoscale was spiking.

liam: job is `deep-scrub-worker-2026-03-10` running as a CronJob -> sees image `redwood/cleaner:2026-02-deepscrub` on nodes gn-21111..21120. logs: 
```
I0310 03:01:05 scrub.go:210] starting deep scrub on /var/tmp/scratch/gn-21114 (dirs=18k, files=560k)
E0310 03:02:17 overlayfs.go:134] overlayfs revalidate failed: -5 IO error on dev nvme2n1
W0310 03:02:18 writeback.go:97] bdi writeback latency spike: 2300ms
E0310 03:03:40 nvme_driver: ctrl_reset: contig read errors=6
```

raj: `overlayfs revalidate failed` + controller reset = bad combination. controller resets will trash IO queue depth and then the scheduler sees ephemeral attach timeouts.

ops-bot: alert created: ap-se1-scratch-iops (1769004350) — average IOQ usage 78% over 2m

sophie: can we throttle the cronjob concurrency immediately and set QoS on cleaner pods?

liam: lowering concurrency: `kubectl patch cronjob deep-scrub-worker -p '{"spec":{"concurrencyPolicy":"Forbid"}}' -n infra` 

autoscale-bot: notice: cluster-autoscaler detected 12 pods pending due to attach timeout in ap-southeast1 at 1769004378

raj: short-term: set `io.bandwidth_limit=20MBps` for cleaner DaemonSet via cgroups and schedule a canary to 2 nodes. Also set `--max-deletes=1000` to avoid giant nukes.

sre-oncall: do it and also mark nvme2n1 on gn-21114 as degraded: schedule local SMART scan and reduce weight for scheduler. I'll open a retire ticket if errors continue.

liam: applied cgroup cap to ds/cleaner on canary nodes. observed IO drop ~65% in 90s and attach waits reduced.

ops-bot: alert cleared: ap-se1-scratch-iops (1769004455)

sophie: medium-term proposal: janitor should consult attach-window lease API to avoid heavy deletes during autoscale events. also prefer nodes with low bdi.writeback_avg.

raj: agree. plus per-device hotness ranking in the scheduler. patch idea: annotate devices with `device.hot=true/false` and have cleaner prefer !hot devices.

liam: note: smartctl returned some reallocated sectors for nvme2n1 (gn-21114). sre-oncall filed INF-2026-462 (nvme-check gn-21114) and kicked off cross-check with hardware team.

sre-oncall: INF-2026-462 created, setting status=investigating. running extended SMART and fio read test now.

sophie: cost note — delaying scrub increases ephemeral tail occupancy; if that pushes steady-state load to Dedicated capacity we'll see a monthly delta. please add a metric for "deferred-scrub-bytes" to the cost dashboard.

liam: added grafana panel and alert if deferred-scrub-bytes > 500GB for 30m.

raj: PR for scheduler + cleaner coordination: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-scheduler/pull/312 (draft) — adds device hotness label and lease API consumer.

liam: follow-ups: promote concurrency cap cluster-wide during autoscale spikes, roll smarter cleaner release with device-ranking, validate SMART scan results for gn-21114 and retire if needed.

sre-oncall: ack, monitoring fio run and will update ticket with results.

sophie: thanks everyone. keep this thread updated when INF-2026-462 changes. :eyes:
